title: AI Daily Briefing
description: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia, open and local models, and AI in defense.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 9–19. New: Anthropic said Nov. 18 that it priced its IPO at $83 a share, with Nasdaq trading expected Nov. 19 under the symbol ANT. Google released Gemini 4 Neon the same day, including a cyber track for the Fairwind Program. Tom's Hardware reported that China's Ministry of Commerce threatened countermeasures after the new AI-chip rental rule. AFRICOM on Nov. 17 described Maven workshops with an Army-led edge super-intelligence team. No new OpenAI model post dated Nov. 18–19 was opened. The Open and Local Models subsection is empty. NVIDIA's revenue figures are on the partners page.

items.headline: OpenAI says automated red teaming made GPT-6 Astra refuse more cyber jailbreaks
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 12 that it used automated red teaming to improve what it calls fuzzy robustness, how reliably a model withholds disallowed help under jailbreak pressure in dual-use areas such as cyber and biology. OpenAI said the method was used to train GPT-6 Astra and Sol, and that on a fixed set of earlier cyber jailbreaks GPT-6 Astra answered 91.5 percent safely, compared with 59 percent for GPT-5.6 Sol. OpenAI said those measurements are of the model without production safeguards, and that deployed high-stakes cyber and biology use still goes through the Daybreak and Rosalind trusted-access programs. OpenAI said the robustness-trained GPT-6 Astra was not more likely to refuse benign tasks.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, with a cyber track for the Fairwind Program
items.summary: Google said Nov. 18 that Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out in the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Gemini for business, Google Antigravity for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers. Google said the price is $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 per million cached input tokens, and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window. Google said Neon scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level, and that at the default high thinking level it costs 32 percent less per task than Gemini 4 Carbon on that index. Google said Neon for cyber is state of the art on SEC-bench Pro at 90.5 percent and on WebExploitBench v1.2 at 51.26 percent, and that eligible Fairwind Program members will begin receiving access over the next few days.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen for faster agentic work, priced below Carbon
items.summary: Google said Nov. 12 that Gemini 4 Hydrogen is available for coding and agentic work in Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, and Google Search. Google said the price is flat across a 1 million-token context window, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, and that at the default high thinking level Hydrogen scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon. Google said Orchestrator in Google Antigravity can switch between Carbon and Hydrogen in one session and, on Terminal-Bench 4.0, reached near-Carbon task success while using 24 percent less quota and finishing 19 percent faster. Google said free users of the Gemini app get Hydrogen through automatic model selection when it fits the prompt.

items.headline: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon generally available and opens a cybersecurity track
items.summary: Google said Nov. 10 that Gemini 4 Carbon is available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers, and that it is the company's strongest model for cybersecurity and long-horizon agentic work. Google said Carbon is priced the same as Gemini 4 Argon during an introductory period, at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, and that the price becomes $4 and $20 after Nov. 30, 2026. Google said Carbon for cyber, available through the Fairwind Program, leads its benchmarks for finding, exploiting, and patching vulnerabilities, and that Google's Cloud Vulnerability Research team used it to show two bugs in a popular open-source project were exploitable at a severity Google compared to PHP2Shell. Google said Wiz, in its Scan for Good program, used Carbon to find zero-days at two major SaaS providers in under two hours.

items.headline: Nvidia says it has agreed to acquire Hugging Face as Vera Rubin ships
items.summary: NVIDIA said Nov. 17, in its fiscal 2027 third-quarter release, that it has agreed to acquire Hugging Face to scale that platform. The same release said Vera Rubin NVL72 has begun shipping, which NVIDIA called the fastest product ramp in its history, with racks running at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and Nebius, and coming online soon at SpaceXSI. NVIDIA said it expanded Anthropic's access to Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin capacity through cloud providers.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: China says it will answer the new AI-chip rental controls
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 18 that China's Ministry of Commerce said China will take countermeasures to safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests after the United States extended export controls on high-end AI accelerator chips. Tom's Hardware said the updated regulation requires licenses to rent those chips in large quantities to Country Group D:5, the list of nations embargoed from arms sales. Tom's Hardware said President Trump is in China for the APEC summit in Shenzhen and is scheduled to meet President Xi Jinping on Nov. 19.

items.headline: BIS issues a rule on remote access to advanced chips through overseas data centers
items.summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security said Nov. 16 that it released an interim final rule, written at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council, so limits on advanced super-intelligence chips cannot be bypassed through remote computing at data centers in third countries. The rule text requires a license to export, reexport, or transfer covered items for a data center, anywhere, that will provide access to more than 12 million aggregate total processing performance to a company headquartered in, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered in, Macau or Country Group D:5. It also requires a license for advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil, with an exception for a U.S.-headquartered consignee that meets a reporting requirement, and it formally rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule, which the preamble says has never been enforced. The displayed text says the rule takes effect on the date it is published in the Federal Register.

items.headline: OpenAI says NATO is using Daybreak models to defend allied networks
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 17 that it works with NATO's Communications and Information Agency to give NATO's core institutions access to advanced cybersecurity models, and that NATO has used up to 300 billion raw input and output tokens per month in that work. OpenAI said it supported the 2026 Crossed Swords exercise, run by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence, where participants built and evaluated AI agents for cyber operations using Daybreak, with an emphasis on human oversight. OpenAI said it has also provided the models to ENISA and to national cyber agencies in France, Germany, and Poland, and that Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation is using Daybreak on civilian infrastructure. NCIA General Manager Dylan Browne said the tools accelerate vulnerability discovery and that NATO will study token consumption and cost as adoption scales.

items.headline: AFRICOM hosts Maven workshops with an Army-led edge super-intelligence team
items.summary: U.S. Africa Command said Nov. 17 that it hosted the Office of the Secretary of War's Chief Data and Analytics Office for workshops in Stuttgart with Maven users from Special Operations Command Africa and AFRICOM's Directorate of Operations. AFRICOM said Maven scans imagery and video, flags information for human analysts, and shows the battlefield on one dashboard, and that the sessions looked for near-term fixes and longer-term needs. A workshop photo is dated Nov. 12 at Kelley Barracks. Army Capt. Ryan T. Hetrick, lead of the Edge Super Intelligence Task Force at the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, said developers have to go where the warfighter works and build alongside the end user.

items.headline: Department of War renames the CDAO the Super Intelligence Office
items.summary: The Department of War said Nov. 13 that it redesignated the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office as the Super Intelligence Office, following President Trump's direction to move federal terminology from artificial intelligence to super intelligence. Cameron Stanley said the office has moved beyond experimental prototypes and that its mission is to harness sovereign super intelligence for military superiority across every domain. The department said the transition will roll out across digital systems, enterprise applications, and component headquarters over the coming weeks, and that existing programs, solicitations, and partnerships continue. Breaking Defense reported the same day that the portfolio includes the Maven Smart System and the War Data Platform, formerly Advana, and that the department launched SI.mil.

items.headline: Air Force applies an AI strategy across 15 mission areas, including nuclear operations
items.summary: Air & Space Forces Magazine reported Nov. 12 that the Department of the Air Force is applying an artificial intelligence strategy across 15 mission areas, from intelligence and human resources to nuclear operations. Chief Data and AI Officer Susan Davenport described the plan at the GovCIO AI Summit on Nov. 6 in Tysons, Virginia, and said each area will be overseen by a general officer or senior civilian who tracks governance and data access. She said the data strategy leaves data with the organizations that produce it, instead of copying it through a central team that tags and cleans it. The department told the magazine the blueprint is controlled unclassified information and was not released, and that domain principals will present roadmaps at a showcase in early 2027.

items.headline: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, with trading expected Nov. 19
items.summary: Anthropic said Nov. 18 that it priced its initial public offering of Class A common stock at $83.00 per share. Anthropic said the offering is 980,000,000 shares, of which 956,351,354 are being sold by the company and 23,648,646 by selling stockholders, and that Anthropic will not receive proceeds from the stockholders' shares. Anthropic said the shares are expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Nov. 19, 2026, under the symbol ANT, and that the offering is expected to close Nov. 20, subject to customary conditions. The Securities and Exchange Commission declared the registration statement effective Nov. 18, and the underwriters have a 30-day option for up to 147,000,000 additional shares.
